ed_visit_unit.question: In NCQA HEDIS Emergency Department Utilization (EDU) and CMS ACO measures, how is an ED visit counted (per encounter, per member-day, per claim)? Is an ED visit that results in inpatient admission counted?
ed_visit_unit.answer: For NCQA HEDIS EDU, the numerator counts **ED visits**, not claims or member-days: each ED visit counts once, and multiple ED visits on the same date count as one; visits resulting in inpatient admission are excluded[9]. For CMS ACO measures, “ACO measures” is not specific enough to give one universal encounter-counting rule: the cited CMS ACO REACH materials describe particular measures, not a general ED-utilization measure[10].

primary_care_visit.question: How do NCQA HEDIS and CMS define a primary care or ambulatory/office visit for measures such as Adults Access to Preventive/Ambulatory Health Services (AAP)? Which visit types count (office, wellness, telehealth)?
primary_care_visit.answer: For HEDIS AAP, a qualifying visit is **not limited to a primary-care office visit**: the specification counts encounters identified by the “Ambulatory Visits,” “Other Ambulatory Visits,” “Telephone Visits,” and “Online Assessments” value sets.[1] This includes qualifying office/outpatient and preventive visits, such as annual wellness visits, as well as eligible synchronous telehealth, telephone, and online-assessment encounters; the billed service must match the specification’s codes.[1][2] Emergency-department and acute inpatient encounters do not count, and laboratory-only claims are excluded.[2][3] AAP defines qualifying ambulatory or preventive care—not the clinician’s specialty—so “primary care” alone is not the test for whether a visit counts.[1]

inpatient_stay.question: How do NCQA HEDIS (Acute Hospital Utilization AHU, Plan All-Cause Readmissions PCR) count inpatient stays: how are transfers and overlapping or same-day admissions combined, and are observation stays included?
inpatient_stay.answer: For **AHU**, observation stays are included; direct transfers among acute inpatient and observation settings count as one discharge, using the final discharge date.[1][3] For **PCR**, observation-only stays are not index hospital stays: acute-to-acute direct transfers count as one stay, retaining the first admission date and last discharge date; stays are distinct when the next admission is at least two calendar days after the prior discharge.[7] A direct transfer is admission to the next setting on the same day as, or the day after, the prior discharge—so same-day admissions qualify.[6][7]

utilization_per_1000.question: In payer and ACO utilization reporting, is "ED visits per 1,000" computed per 1,000 members (headcount) or per 1,000 member-years (member months/12)? What do HEDIS EDU and CMS use?
utilization_per_1000.answer: “ED visits per 1,000” depends on the specification: when exposure is meant to account for enrollment duration, the denominator is member-years—typically member months ÷ 12—not a simple headcount. HEDIS EDU is **not** a standard visits-per-1,000 measure: it reports a risk-adjusted observed-to-expected ratio; NCQA’s utilization-rate convention uses member-years for commercial/Medicare and member-months for Medicaid.[1][3] CMS ACO REACH reports outpatient ED visits per 1,000 **person-years**.[2][6] CMS also publishes other ED measures explicitly per 1,000 beneficiaries, so check the particular metric’s definition before comparing rates.[5]

ckd_definition.question: For population health registries and CMS chronic condition definitions, does chronic kidney disease include diabetic kidney disease (ICD-10 E11.2x/E11.22) and ESRD (N18.6)? Which ICD-10 codes define CKD in the CMS Chronic Conditions Data Warehouse?
ckd_definition.answer: Yes. CMS’s CCW Chronic Kidney Disease algorithm includes diabetic kidney disease codes **E11.21, E11.22, and E11.29** (along with analogous codes for other diabetes types), and it includes **N18.6** for end-stage renal disease.[1] The algorithm’s CKD code set is broader than the N18 stage codes: it also lists specified diabetes, hypertension, and other kidney-disease codes; it requires qualifying claims over two years.[1]

heart_failure_definition.question: Which ICD-10 codes define heart failure in the CMS Chronic Conditions Warehouse and HEDIS value sets? Are hypertensive heart disease with heart failure (I11.0, I13.0) included?
heart_failure_definition.answer: The CMS CCW’s current “Heart Failure and Non-Ischemic Heart Disease” algorithm includes **I09.81, I11.0, I13.0, I13.2, I42.0, I42.5–I42.8, I43, I50.1, I50.20–I50.23, I50.30–I50.33, I50.40–I50.43, I50.810–I50.814, I50.82–I50.84, I50.89, I50.9, and P29.0**; it uses a two-year lookback and specified qualifying claims.[1] **Yes: both I11.0 and I13.0 are explicitly included** (as is I13.2).[1] “HEDIS value sets” do not define one universal heart-failure code list; the applicable codes depend on the specific measure and measurement-year specification, so the available official NCQA reference does not establish that I11.0 and I13.0 are included in every HEDIS heart-failure value set.[2]

diabetes_a1c_control.question: In NCQA HEDIS Glycemic Status Assessment for Patients With Diabetes (GSD, formerly HbA1c control), what counts: the most recent A1c in the measurement year, and how are patients with no test handled (counted as poor control?)
diabetes_a1c_control.answer: Use the most recent HbA1c **or GMI result from the measurement year**; if more than one assessment occurs on the same date, use the lowest result.[3] GSD reports two rates: <8.0% and >9.0%.[8] A missing result or no assessment is **not** treated as poor control in the sense of an observed >9% value, but it is counted as numerator-compliant for the >9% indicator; for the <8% indicator, it is not numerator-compliant.[3]

readmission_30d.question: How does CMS / NCQA HEDIS Plan All-Cause Readmissions define a 30-day readmission: index stay exclusions, planned readmissions, and day counting from discharge?
readmission_30d.answer: In NCQA HEDIS PCR, the index is an acute inpatient or observation stay discharged during the measurement year; exclude stays ending in death, with a principal discharge diagnosis of pregnancy or a perinatal condition, and stays not meeting the measure’s eligibility/date rules.[1][3] A readmission is an **unplanned** acute inpatient or observation admission for any diagnosis within 30 days; planned stays identified by the specification’s criteria are not counted, and an index stay is excluded when its first readmission is planned.[1][2][10] The window is based on the **readmission admission date**: it must fall within 30 days after the index discharge date; the discharge day is day zero, so the next calendar day is day one.[2]

follow_up_after_ed.question: What are the NCQA HEDIS Follow-Up After Emergency Department Visit measures (FMC for multiple chronic conditions): which follow-up visit types count and within how many days?
follow_up_after_ed.answer: FMC counts a follow-up service on the ED date or within **7 days after the ED visit**—an eight-day window including the ED date.[2][3] Qualifying types include outpatient visits; telehealth or telephone visits; e-visits or virtual check-ins; transitional-care management, case-management, or complex-care-management visits; outpatient or telehealth behavioral-health visits; intensive outpatient or partial-hospitalization encounters; community mental-health-center visits; observation visits; and substance-use-disorder counseling or services.[3]

no_show_rate.question: What is the standard definition of an appointment no-show rate in ambulatory practice operations: denominator (all scheduled, or kept plus no-shows), and are same-day cancellations counted?
no_show_rate.answer: There is no single universal denominator: it depends on the reporting specification. A clear ambulatory operational specification (AAMC/Vizient) defines the rate as patient no-shows **plus patient cancellations on the appointment day or day before**, divided by that numerator **plus completed appointments**—so it excludes earlier cancellations and is not “all originally scheduled” appointments[1]. Other specifications use true no-shows only and exclude cancellations from scheduled appointments, so report the cancellation window and formula explicitly[8].
